content.text:
Fixed and committed (`9bb88b0`). Nothing now counts after "~logged out~" until you hit "Resume tracking".

**Cause:** the `~logged out~` marker was filtered out before spans were built. The Mac stayed awake, so the last project or Break kept stretching through the evening, as in your screenshot.

**Fix:** new `TimeCalculations.applyLogouts` in `TimeCalculations.swift`, used by the day menu, the week timeline and the report. Between logout and resume it:
- drops screen events and project entries
- closes the screen with an `off` at the logout time
- gives the time before logout to the project that was running
- on resume, inserts a Break so the logged-out gap doesn't count

If you never resume, the day simply ends at logout. After a resume, the time from logout to resume shows as a Break block in the timeline.

Two tests cover logout and resume, and the build is clean. I also ran the existing suite: 39 tests pass, but only with `-Xswiftc -swift-version -Xswiftc 5`. Plain `swift test` fails to build on a clean tree because of a Swift 6 Sendable error in `TimeCalculatorTests.swift`, which I left alone.

I haven't rebuilt or restarted the app (`./build.sh` and `./restart.sh`), so the running instance doesn't have this yet. Your past days still contain the logout markers and should show corrected totals once you restart.
